ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word comes last in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. aunt
   B. brother
   C. sister
   D. uncle

2. Which article goes before 'uniform'? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. the
   C. an
   D. one

3. Which sentence is wrong? (1 mark)
   A. I have an books.
   B. I have the book.
   C. I have a book.
   D. I have books.

4. Which information is a school detail? (1 mark)
   A. Your date of birth
   B. Your favourite food
   C. Name of the head teacher
   D. Your weight

5. What does 'DOB' mean on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Duty of boy
   B. Day of business
   C. Date of birth
   D. Date of book

6. Which pair is a minimal pair for /l/ and /r/? (1 mark)
   A. bird, girl
   B. lake, rake
   C. five, nine
   D. boy, toy

7. Which question is indirect? (1 mark)
   A. When did the girl cry?
   B. Where did she cry?
   C. Why do you think the girl cried?
   D. Who cried?

8. Which noun is always plural? (1 mark)
   A. book
   B. spoon
   C. scissors
   D. cup

9. Which sentence has correct capital letters and the correct ending? (1 mark)
   A. We went to Mombasa on Saturday,
   B. We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
   C. We went to Mombasa on Saturday?
   D. We went to mombasa on saturday

10. What do we say when someone thanks us? (1 mark)
   A. Congratulations
   B. I beg your pardon
   C. Excuse me
   D. You are welcome

11. What do we say when a friend wins a prize? (1 mark)
   A. I beg your pardon
   B. Good night
   C. Excuse me
   D. Congratulations

12. In 'The Purse in the Market', what did Neema do with the purse? (1 mark)
   A. She sold it
   B. She kept it
   C. She threw it away
   D. She returned it to its owner

13. 'He is old enough to ride a bicycle.' Here enough comes (1 mark)
   A. after the adjective
   B. before the verb
   C. at the end
   D. before the noun

14. In the pattern 'enough + noun + to + verb', the word after 'to' is a (1 mark)
   A. verb
   B. noun
   C. adjective
   D. name

15. Which letter is silent in 'knife'? (1 mark)
   A. f
   B. e
   C. n
   D. k

16. Why should there be a gap between words? (1 mark)
   A. So that the words are easy to read
   B. To hide mistakes
   C. To use more paper
   D. To make the page dirty

17. In the word 'hospital', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. None
   B. The first
   C. The second
   D. The third

18. Which word goes before a noun to show ownership? (1 mark)
   A. yours
   B. my
   C. hers
   D. mine

19. Listening and diet: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. good
   B. food
   C. book
   D. foot

20. Which is a good rule for a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. Talk all the time
   B. Take books home and keep them
   C. Tear pages
   D. Listen politely and take turns

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy. (4 marks)

22. In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain? (2 marks)

23. Write two minimal pairs for /l/ and /r/. (2 marks)

24. Name two visuals you can find in a newspaper. (2 marks)

25. Give two reasons why we should read widely. (2 marks)

26. Explain how you can tell b from d when you write. (2 marks)

27. Write the plurals of: bus, story, wolf, mouse. (2 marks)

28. Fill in this form line with your own details in block letters: Name, Grade, School. (Write an example.) (3 marks)

29. Describe how to find facts about a lion in a junior encyclopaedia. (4 marks)

30. Write the greeting and closing for a friendly letter to your friend Wanjiku. (2 marks)

31. Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread. (3 marks)

32. Write the subject and the object forms of: I, he, we, they. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — uncle
   u comes after a, b and s.

2. A — a
   Uniform starts with the consonant sound 'yoo'.

3. A — I have an books.
   A and an cannot be used before a plural noun.

4. C — Name of the head teacher
   School details include the school name, address and teachers.

5. C — Date of birth
   DOB is short for date of birth.

6. B — lake, rake
   Lake and rake differ only in the first sound.

7. C — Why do you think the girl cried?
   The answer must be worked out from clues.

8. C — scissors
   Scissors are two blades joined together, so the noun is plural.

9. B — We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
   Sentences start with a capital letter and names such as Mombasa and Saturday also need capitals.

10. D — You are welcome
   You are welcome is the polite reply.

11. D — Congratulations
   Congratulations shows we are happy for someone.

12. D — She returned it to its owner
   Neema found the woman and returned the purse.

13. A — after the adjective
   With adjectives, enough comes after the adjective.

14. A — verb
   To is followed by a verb such as sit or eat.

15. D — k
   We say nife, so the k is silent.

16. A — So that the words are easy to read
   Gaps make the writing legible.

17. B — The first
   We say HOS-pi-tal.

18. B — my
   My comes before a noun. Mine stands alone.

19. B — food
   Food has /uː/. The others have /ʊ/.

20. D — Listen politely and take turns
   Politeness keeps everyone included.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: light, right and load, road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: photographs, cartoons, maps, charts, advertisements.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary and improves reading speed and understanding. It gives knowledge and enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: b: stick first then the round part on the right. d: round part first then the stick on the right.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each letter.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: buses, stories, wolves, mice
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name: AMINA NJOROGE; Grade: 4; School: SUNRISE PRIMARY SCHOOL (any correct example).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line in block letters.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the topic Lion, find the L volume or type it in the search box, use guide words or the index to find the page, read the text, pictures and captions and write short notes in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dear Wanjiku, ... Yours lovingly, (your name).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the greeting with comma and 1 mark for the closing.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: I, me; he, him; we, us; they, them.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each pair.
